svg.data-weight-note: 21.5 kg (47.4 lb) with 2 PSUs and 4 fans installed - both documents agree
svg.data-mac-addresses: 8K exact match, 128K without exact match (subject to NOS)
svg.data-power-budget-per-port-w: 24 on ports 1-4, 29-36 and 61-64; 13 on all other ports
svg.data-operating-temp: 0 to 40 C (32 to 104 F) at sea level; 0 to 35 C (32 to 95 F) at 1828 m
svg.data-software: ONIE preloaded; compatible with Open Network Linux and Enterprise SONiC by Edgecore
svg.data-optics-qsfp-dd: datasheet: each QSFP56-DD port takes 1 x 400G QSFP56-DD, 1 x 100G QSFP28 or 1 x 40G QSFP+, or breaks out to 2 x 200G (2 x 4 lanes 50G PAM4), 4 x 100G (4 x 2 lanes 50G PAM4), 2 x 50G (2 x 2 lanes 25G NRZ), 4 x 25G NRZ or 4 x 10G NRZ. The guide's lamp legend lists the same set and adds the 1 x 8 lanes 50G PAM4 mode for 400G.
svg.data-dac-reach: datasheet interfaces table: the sixteen 24 W ports "Support 400G QSFP56-DD DAC up to 2.5m" and the other forty-eight "up to 1m". The extra watts buy reach.
svg.data-emissions: EN 55032 Class A, EN 61000-3-2, EN 61000-3-3, VCCI-CISPR 32 Class A, AS/NZS CISPR 32 Class A, ICES-003 Issue 7 Class A, FCC Class A

There is only one ordering code, so this is also the only build.","kind":"base"}},"description":"64 x 400G QSFP56-DD 2RU spine switch on a Broadcom Tomahawk 4 with an Intel Xeon D-1548, sold as the DCS520 and stamped AS9736-64D. ALL PORTS ARE ON THE FRONT in TWO BANKS OF SIXTEEN STACKED COLUMNS, numbered from 1, with the legend `N (up)(down) N+1` printed BETWEEN the two cages of each column. Two 10G SFP+ management cages at the left are ports 65 and 66; five system lamps stand in a column above them; an RJ-45 console, an RJ-45 management jack and a USB Type-A stack at the right. SIXTEEN OF THE SIXTY-FOUR ARE 24 W PORTS and the datasheet names them one by one. It is the fourth device on the 440 x 649.2 x 87 shell and THE ONLY ONE OF THE FOUR WHOSE REAR PUTS A SUPPLY AT EACH END with the four fan trays between them - the AIS800-64D, the AIS800-64O and the AGR560 all stack two supplies at the left. One shell, two rear architectures.","format":1,"gaps":[{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["rear"],"wanted":"A FAN FRU NUMBER FOR THIS MODEL. `edgecore/dcs520-fan@1` was written as its own part and it very probably is not one: the three other devices on this shell all seat a tray whose FRU number `FAN-2U-1x1SN-F` is printed in all three of their datasheets, and this machine's trays sit on a mean pitch of 85.58 against their uniform 85.71 - thirteen hundredths of a millimetre - with the same honeycomb, the same angled red bar with two pairs of slots and a central button, and the same corner lamp. THE MEASUREMENTS ARGUE FOR ONE PART MEASURED TWICE, NOT FOR TWO PARTS. The three gaps here run 85.54, 85.64 and 85.55, a spread of a tenth of a millimetre, where the other three chassis repeat 85.71 with no spread at all; and this face is 80.1 x 83.5 `measured` against the shared tray's 81.6 x 81.2 `photo-measured`, a disagreement of 1.5 x 2.3 mm. Irregular spacing and a face that misses by more than the pitch does are what pixel-measuring a drawing produces beside a dimensioned source. Two rulers, not two trays. NEITHER DCS520 DOCUMENT PRINTS A FAN PART NUMBER, so the argument that settled the other three is unavailable, and the drawings cannot settle it either: scaled to a common size and normalised, 46% of pixels differ by more than a standard deviation, but that is this guide drawing the tray bright with the rotor showing through the mesh against the AIS800 guides drawing it dark. A test that cannot tell a different part from different lighting decides nothing. One FRU list closes this. If it names `FAN-2U-1x1SN-F`, delete this component and seat the shared one.","what":"fan-tray-identity"},{"reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["front"],"wanted":"WHERE THE RESET BUTTON IS. The datasheet's System and Port LEDs section ends with the bare line \"Reset button\", and neither document draws one that can be found: the guide's Overview callouts run 1-9 and none of them is a button, its System/Port LEDs enlargements cover the left end, the port field and the right cluster without showing one, and at 8.87 px/mm the datasheet photograph resolves the pinholes it does have - the grounding screws, the PSU status lamps - without any obvious candidate on the port side. So the device is modelled without it rather than with one guessed onto a plausible patch of metal. An enlargement of either end of the front panel closes this.","what":"the-reset-button"},{"reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["front"],"wanted":"THE EXACT OFFSET OF THE LANE-LAMP STRIP FROM ITS CAGE. Four lamps per port is stated outright by the guide, the strip is visible on the posts in its enlargements, and its HEIGHT measures well - about 10.85 mm over four windows on a 3.5 mm pitch, which is why `common/qsfp-lane-leds-column@1` fits it. Its x is the soft number: the enlargement puts the strip about 10.7 mm right of the column centre while the post it stands in spans 9.05 to 14.8, and the panel's two scales - 11.94 px/mm read across the columns against 10.53 read down the rows - do not agree well enough to choose inside that range. 11.0 is used and the render was checked against the reference at matched scale. A dimensioned faceplate drawing, or one enlargement with a known length in it, closes it.","what":"port-lamp-strip-position"}],"groups":{"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"3+1","redundancy-note":"datasheet, three times over - key features, physical section and interfaces table: \"3 + 1 redundant, hot-swappable fan modules\". FOUR BAYS AND THE FIGURE COUNTS BAYS, which is not true of the two AIS800 models on this same shell, where a \"7+1\" counts eight rotors inside four trays. Same chassis, same tray size, two different things counted."},"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Part"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"Point"},"leds":{"index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the machine's management interfaces. TWO 10G SFP+ CAGES at the left of the face, which both documents call management ports and which the panel numbers 65 and 66 - into the same sequence as the sixty-four traffic ports, labelled above and below their block rather than between its rows. Then, stacked vertically at the right of the face, an RJ-45 console port, a 10/100/1000M RJ-45 management port whose own lamps the guide legends \"Left: link, Right: activity\", and a USB storage port. THE SFP+ PAIR IS WRITTEN LONGHAND rather than generated, because a block would set each port's position in its group from its printed number and these two are 65 and 66 in a group of five. WHAT RUNS IN THEM: 10G SFP+, with the guide's lamp legend giving them 10G and 1G states - \"Left: Green (10G link), Amber (1G link); Right: Green (10G activity), Amber (1G activity)\". No optics table is published for this pair and none is invented; it is recorded here rather than as an `optics-` attribute because these cages are in the management group, which is what both documents call them.","role":"management","term":"Port"},"port-leds":{"index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"psus":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"datasheet: \"PSUs: 2 redundant, load-sharing, hot-swappable 2400 W AC/HVDC power supplies\", each 2400 W against a stated maximum draw of 2100 W. AT 200-240 VAC OR 240 VDC THAT IS A GENUINE 1+1 and the guide says one supply will do: \"install one or two AC PSUs\". AT 100-127 VAC IT IS NOT - \"two AC PSUs must be installed\" - so the claim here is the high-line one. THE TWO ARE MOUNTED THE OPPOSITE WAY UP from each other, which is the guide's own instruction rather than a drawing artefact: \"PSU 1 AC socket faces down, and PSU 2 AC socket faces up.\""},"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"qsfp56dd":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp-dd","speed":"400g"},"description":"the sixty-four 400G QSFP56-DD ports, in TWO BANKS OF SIXTEEN STACKED COLUMNS on a single 23.868 mm pitch with no ganging - ports 1-32 the upper bank and 33-64 the lower, numbered down each column from 1 at the top left, with the legend `N (up)(down) N+1` printed BETWEEN the two cages of its column. SIXTEEN OF THEM ARE 24 W PORTS - 1-4, 29-36 and 61-64, the first two and last two columns of each bank - and the datasheet names them individually. The other forty-eight are 13 W. The extra watts buy DAC reach: 2.5 m against 1 m.","index-origin":1,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"Edgecore","maturity":"modelled","model":"AS9736-64D","name":"dcs520","portfolio":{"family":"Data Center Switch","line":"Cloud Data Center","series":"DCS520"},"profile":"networking","provenance":{"four-lamps-a-port-and-the-count-lit-is-the-breakout":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"THE GUIDE PRINTS THE WHOLE VOCABULARY and it is unusual enough to transcribe in full, QSFP56-DD LEDs: 400G (1x8 lanes 50G PAM4) = 1 lamp blue; 200G (2x4 lanes 50G PAM4) = 2 cyan; 100G (4x2 lanes 50G PAM4) = 4 green; 100G (1x4 lanes 25G NRZ) = 1 green; 40G (1x4 lanes 10G NRZ) = 1 dark green; 50G (2x2 lanes 25G NRZ) = 2 red; 25G (4x1 lane 25G NRZ) = 4 orange; 10G (4x1 lane 10G NRZ) = 4 yellow. SO THE NUMBER OF LAMPS LIT IS THE BREAKOUT AND THE COLOUR IS THE RATE - four lamps per port, one per lane group, not one lamp per port. The guide's enlargement shows exactly that: a vertical strip of four diamond windows on the post beside each cage, measured about 10.85 mm tall on a 3.5 mm pitch. `common/qsfp-lane-leds-column@1` IS THAT PART - 1.8 x 11.4, four lane elements stacked vertically - and it is already seated by the sibling dcs510. 64 ports x 4 is 256 port lamps on this face. THE OTHER TWO LEGENDS, same page: \"SFP+ 10G LEDs: Left: Green (10G link), Amber (1G link); Right: Green (10G activity), Amber (1G activity)\" and \"RJ-45 MGMT LEDs: Left: Green (1G link), Amber (10/100M link); Right: Green (1G activity), Amber (10/100M activity)\"."},"gate-1":{"confidence":"measured","note":"FOUR CANDIDATE INSTRUMENTS WERE MEASURED BEFORE ONE WAS CHOSEN, and three pass. The guide's FRONT elevation reads 2217 x 441 px - 5.0386 px/mm across 440 and 5.0690 down 87, -0.598% apart. Its REAR reads 2222 x 442: 5.0500 and 5.0805, -0.600%. The datasheet's FRONT photograph reads 3901 x 776: 8.8659 and 8.9195, -0.601%, which is 1.76x the guide and is the primary instrument for the port wall. THREE INSTRUMENTS AGREEING ON ASPECT TO 0.003% is one CAD source seen three ways, and it is worth saying that the agreed figure is -0.6% rather than zero: the drawings are consistently a little wide for 440 x 87, and that bias is in all of them. THE DATASHEET'S REAR PHOTOGRAPH FAILS at -1.33% and was NOT discarded but recalibrated: its bbox includes the rack-ear tabs that stand proud of the body top and bottom, so rear measurements taken on it are scaled on the chassis width alone and every number is a feature measurement. The guide's rear elevation is the rear's primary instrument."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"TWO 2400 W SUPPLIES against a stated draw of \"287.75 W (min.), 2100 W (max.)\". Input ratings: \"100-127 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 12 A maximum; 200-240 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 15 A maximum; HVDC: 240 VDC, 15 A maximum\". THE 1+1 CLAIM IS A HIGH-LINE CLAIM and the guide says so: at 200-240 VAC or 240 VDC one or two AC PSUs may be fitted, but at 100-127 VAC both AC PSUs are required. At low line the pair is not redundant. THE INLET IS A SAF-D-GRID AND THE C20 IS THE WALL END OF THE CORD. The datasheet says \"AC PSU Inlet: Anderson Saf D Grid\"; the guide's package contents list an \"HVAC/IEC C20 1m power cord\" and the ordering table an \"HVAC to IEC 60320 C20 (1m)\". Reading the C20 as the inlet would put the wrong connector on the supply's face."},"sources":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"A THREE-PAGE QUICK START GUIDE AND A FOUR-PAGE DATASHEET, and between them they cover this device well. The guide carries the Overview elevations of both faces, a System/Port LEDs page whose three enlargement panels are the instrument for the lamps and the numbering, the FRU replacement steps and the specification table. The datasheet carries photographs of both faces, the interfaces table, the power ratings, the per-port power list and the single ordering code. THE STAGED PHOTOGRAPHS ARE USELESS AND WERE NOT USED: four files at 489 x 357 px over a 440 mm face is 1.1 px/mm. Everything below is measured on 600 dpi PAGE RENDERS."},"stack-orientation":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 32 QSFP-DD pairs (port-1/port-2 to port-63/port-64), the 1 SFP pair (port-65/port-66)."},"the-numbering-starts-at-one-and-the-legend-sits-between-the-rows":{"confidence":"measured","note":"`N (up)(down) N+1` IS PRINTED BETWEEN THE TWO CAGES OF ITS COLUMN, in white on the bare panel. There are NO COLOURED BANDS anywhere on this face - which is a real difference from the AGR560 on the same shell, whose whole numbering scheme is coloured bands, and from the AIS800 pair, which print their legends above and below their banks rather than inside them. NUMBERING STARTS AT 1, not 0. Read on the guide's enlargements, which resolve `1 (up)(down) 2`, `3 (up)(down) 4`, `33 (up)(down) 34`, `35 (up)(down) 36`, `61 (up)(down) 62` and `63 (up)(down) 64` - both ends of both banks. SO EACH BANK IS ONE BLOCK OF THIRTY-TWO. Column-major, i = col*2 + row, gives n = 1 + i exactly: column k carries 2k+1 and 2k+2. That is the opposite of the AGR560, whose stride of four forced twelve separate blocks. THE SFP+ PAIR IS NUMBERED INTO THE SAME SEQUENCE as ports 65 and 66, labelled above and below their block rather than between them."},"the-port-wall":{"confidence":"measured","note":"SIXTY-FOUR QSFP56-DD IN TWO BANKS OF SIXTEEN STACKED COLUMNS - ports 1-32 in the upper bank and 33-64 in the lower - which is the AIS800-64D's architecture on the same shell. THE COLUMN PITCH WAS FITTED THREE TIMES, on three separate rows of the datasheet photograph, by least squares over all sixteen columns: 23.8605 (row 2), 23.8648 (row 3) and 23.8779 (row 4), with first centres of 39.25, 39.27 and 39.18. Three independent fits inside 0.017 mm of each other is one pitch: 23.868 from 39.23. THERE IS NO GANGING and the residuals say so. They are all under 0.6 mm and they BOW smoothly - positive at both ends of the face, negative in the middle - which is the photograph's own lens distortion. A ganged block shows residuals that ALTERNATE, and these do not. THE ROWS WERE MEASURED ON THE CAGE BEZELS, not on the openings. The bezel is a continuous bright line; the opening is dark, textured and merges with its neighbours at 5 px/mm. On the guide's elevation the eight bezel lines read 11.64-20.81, 25.74-35.02, 52.18-61.45 and 66.38-75.76, giving row centres 16.23, 30.38, 56.82 and 71.07 and cages 9.17 to 9.38 tall. ONE ROW PITCH IS USED FOR BOTH BANKS. Fitted separately they give 14.15 (upper) and 14.25 (lower) - a tenth of a millimetre apart, which is half a pixel on this elevation - and the hardware is plainly one cage assembly used twice, exactly as the AIS800-64D's 17.61 and 17.41 were merged. 14.20 is the mean. THE DRAWN OPENING IS 18.0 TO 18.3 WIDE against std/qsfp-dd@1's registry 19.0, the same bias every device in this family records: the registry owns the aperture and the device owns the pitch."},"the-rear-is-the-familys-shell-and-nobody-elses-architecture":{"confidence":"measured","note":"ONE SUPPLY AT EACH END, FOUR FAN TRAYS BETWEEN THEM. The three other devices on this shell stack both supplies at the left. Measured on the guide's rear elevation, in two horizontal bands chosen clear of the handles so that the seams are found twice: seam pairs at 45.45/51.39, 131.49/136.93, 217.13/222.57, 302.77/308.12 and 388.42/394.26. Fan bays 80.1 wide on a pitch of 85.65 - 85.64, 85.64, 85.65 on the three intervals. THE SUPPLIES ARE TALL AND NARROW: 39.7 x 53.3, measured on the datasheet photograph on the module's own rails, not the family's 73.5 x 40 CRPS brick. THE TWO SUPPLIES ARE MIRRORED AND THE GUIDE STATES IT: \"Install the replacement PSU in a matching orientation. (PSU 1 AC socket faces down, and PSU 2 AC socket faces up.)\" The elevation agrees independently - PSU 1's internal features cluster at y 34.4-65.9 and PSU 2's at 20.5-37.8, and they map onto each other by reflection about the chassis mid-height to within 0.6 mm. So one component is seated twice and the second is turned through 180 degrees. THE GROUNDING PLATE STAYS AT THE BOTTOM ON BOTH SIDES and is therefore chassis, not supply: the guide's callout 7 is \"2 x grounding screws (maximum torque 10 kgf-cm (8.7 lb-in))\" and there is one under each supply."},"the-system-lamps-are-five-and-an-early-misreading-is-worth-recording":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"LOC, STAT, FAN, PSU1, PSU2 - five, in a VERTICAL column at the top left with the label to the left of each lamp, on a 3.0 mm pitch. THE STATES ARE GIVEN: LOC flashing blue/amber = switch locator; STAT green = OK, blinking green = system booting, amber = fault; FAN green = OK, amber = fault, blinking amber = too few fans installed; PSU1/PSU2 green = OK, amber = fault. AN EARLY READING OF THE DATASHEET PHOTOGRAPH AS \"DIAG, FAN, LOC, PSU1, PSU2\" WAS WRONG and is recorded because the mistake is instructive. That silkscreen is about four pixels tall in the photograph; enlarged nine times it resolves into five blurred four-character words and nothing more. The QSG's enlargement prints the names legibly, the QSG's own legend text lists the same five, and the datasheet's PROSE says \"System LEDs: PSU1, PSU2, FAN, STAT, and LOC\". Three sources agree and the fourth was never readable - there is no disagreement here, only a misreading of blur."},"the-twenty-four-watt-ports-are-named-one-by-one":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"Ports 1-4, 29-36 and 61-64 = 24 W per transceiver; every other port = 13 W per transceiver - the datasheet's power section, and the interfaces table splits the face the same way: \"16 x 400G QSFP56-DD ports (24W) Support 400G QSFP56-DD DAC up to 2.5m\" against \"48 x 400G QSFP56-DD ports (13W) ... up to 1m\". THAT IS THE FIRST TWO AND LAST TWO COLUMNS OF EACH BANK, which is exactly what the datasheet photograph's three yellow highlight boxes mark - two columns, twelve columns, two columns. A stated fact and a drawn one agreeing, so the per-port attribute below is not an inference."}},"references":[{"title":"Edgecore DCS520 / AS9736-64D Quick Start Guide"},{"title":"Edgecore DCS520 / AS9736-64D Datasheet"}],"version":"1.0.7","views":{"bottom":{"empty":"Not drawn by any staged source. g.data-description: the sixty-four 400G QSFP56-DD ports, in TWO BANKS OF SIXTEEN STACKED COLUMNS on a single 23.868 mm pitch with no ganging - ports 1-32 the upper bank and 33-64 the lower, numbered down each column from 1 at the top left, with the legend `N (up)(down) N+1` printed BETWEEN the two cages of its column. SIXTEEN OF THEM ARE 24 W PORTS - 1-4, 29-36 and 61-64, the first two and last two columns of each bank - and the datasheet names them individually. The other forty-eight are 13 W. The extra watts buy DAC reach: 2.5 m against 1 m.
